title: Fix inline R span closing
description:
Inline knitr chunks like `r format(...)` never closed because the embedded R syntax's prototypes intercept the closing backtick before `code-span-knitr` can see it. Adding a `with_prototype` lookahead that pops when the matching backtick is ahead ensures the existing `(?!`)` rule fires.

This restores highlighting for inline R expressions without affecting the embedded R parsing.

title: Fix cell, inline and math highlighting; add divs and shortcodes
description:
## Summary

Fixes several highlighting bugs, most visibly inline R code colouring the rest of the document. It also migrates the syntax to `version: 2`, adds Quarto constructs that had no highlighting, and adds a syntax test. Everything was checked on Sublime Text Build 4215, and Pandoc behaviour was checked with Quarto's bundled Pandoc (`quarto pandoc -f markdown -t native`).

Fixes #2 and fixes #6. For #2 this covers the original report, the `_` in an include path; the escaping problem described in a later comment there was not checked.

## Bugs fixed

- **Inline code ran on past its span.** Inline R code (`` `r x` ``) was included rather than embedded, so R's own contexts could hold the span open and the rest of the document was highlighted as R. `code-span-knitr` now embeds the language with an escape on the closing backticks, which wins at any nesting depth. It also covers `` `{r} x` ``, `` `{python} x` `` and `` `{julia} x` ``. An unterminated span ends at the next blank line. This is the same bug as #5, fixed a different way; the two edit the same rule and will conflict.
- **A `"```"` string closed a cell.** The cell escape was a bare `` (```) ``. It now needs the backticks alone on their line, at least as many as opened the cell, so four-backtick cells can contain three-backtick lines.
- **Four-backtick and indented cells were not highlighted.** Cells inside list items are now recognised too.
- **LaTeX math lost its highlighting (#6).** The math rules included contexts that no longer exist in the bundled LaTeX syntax. Math now uses `text.tex.latex#math-content`, and `\begin{equation}` and `\begin{align}` bodies get math scopes up to the matching `\end`.
- **An unbalanced quote in heading or div attributes**, such as `## Title {a="b}`, coloured everything up to the next quote in the file. Attributes now end at the end of their line.
- **The `_` in a shortcode such as `{{< include _part.qmd >}}` started italics (#2).**

## Added

- **Fenced divs**, with attributes (`::: {.callout-note}`) or a bare class name (`::: warning`). At top level a marker only counts at column 0, matching Pandoc: an indented `:::` stays code or text. Inside list items any indent is accepted, as Pandoc does. Only a column-0 closing `:::` ends a paragraph.
- **Heading attributes** (`## Heading {#sec-id .class}`).
- **Shortcodes** (`{{< name args >}}`), with string arguments. The name uses `support.function` rather than `entity.name.function`, so shortcodes do not appear in Goto Symbol.
- **Cells:** these languages each get their own body scope: r and Rscript, python, julia, sql, bash and sh, Rcpp, ojs, dot, `=html`, `=latex` and `=tex`. A leading dot, as in `{.python}`, is handled the same way. Any other language, including mermaid, falls back to plain.
- **`\@`** now escapes a citation.
- **`syntax_test_quarto.qmd`**, with 50 assertions covering the cases above.

## Version 2

`version: 2` changes how `embed_scope` combines with the embedded syntax's scope, so every `embed_scope` now names that scope explicitly. Per-character scopes before and after the migration were compared over a test document and differed only where intended.

## Behaviour changes to be aware of

- A cell header's `{` and language name now carry the cell's `markup.raw.code-fence.*` scope, as the rest of the header already did.
- Julia is not bundled with Sublime. Without a Julia package the console logs `Unable to find syntax file for scope "source.julia"` when the syntax loads. The current release already logs this. Keeping the reference means Julia highlights once a Julia package is installed. The README now says so.

## Known limitations

- Fenced divs inside block quotes are not recognised.
- A bare `:::` outside any div ends a paragraph, though Pandoc keeps it as text, because the syntax does not track div nesting.

## Testing

With the checkout at `Packages/Quarto`, open `syntax_test_quarto.qmd` and run **Tools > Build** with the Syntax Tests build system. On Build 4215: 50 assertions, 0 failures.

Front matter is not in the syntax test: it is only recognised on line 1, which the test header occupies. It was checked by tokenising a document instead.
